speaker: village
text: Year 10: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Ryn, Roan to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Bram is dead and Taric is dead, and the pile's got fifteen for twelve of us — that's more breathing room than we've had in years, but I want us at the pile early before Mako decides this is the year he stops being polite about it. Ryn, you're at zero food coming out of last year and that doesn't stand; Roan, same question I always ask you: how hungry are you walking into this morning?

speaker: a010
text: Hungry enough that I ate nothing last year and I'm still standing, which tells me I've been leaning on Eron longer than a father should. I'll be at the pile early — two food is what I need to keep breathing, and I won't reach past that. What are you thinking about Mako?

speaker: a011
text: Mako's sitting on zero food same as Ryn, which means he's going to the pile hungry and a hungry Mako is unpredictable — but he's also got Zinn and a daughter's loyalty pulling at him, so he's not going to do anything that makes the whole village turn cold on him the year after Bram died proving what that costs. Ryn, you take two from the pile before anyone counts you out, and Roan, you take your two and don't wait to see who moves first. I'll be right behind both of you.

speaker: a010
text: Dell's read on Mako sounds right to me — a man who watched Bram die on the wrong side of a circle isn't going to make the same mistake the same year. I'll take my two and step back; the pile's generous enough today that nobody should be reaching past fair share, and I'd rather spend this morning watching who lingers at the edge than counting my own food.

speaker: a011
text: Ryn, I want to hear your voice in this before we walk out that door — you've been quiet since I named Mako, and quiet from you in a room like this means you're holding something I should know before the pile opens.

speaker: a010
text: Ryn, if you've got something sitting behind your teeth, this is the room for it — Dell and I aren't going anywhere yet, and I'd rather know what's bothering you now than piece it together from how you move at the pile.

speaker: a011
text: Ryn's gone quiet twice in this conversation and neither of us has heard a word from her — that silence is the thing I'm holding right now, Roan, and if she doesn't speak before this room closes I'm going to take two from the pile and then stand next to her until she does, because a woman who's fed me through every lean year I've known doesn't go quiet without a reason worth hearing.

speaker: a010
text: Ryn, Dell's been carrying you the same way Eron's been carrying me, and neither of us can afford to walk into this year blind — so say what you've got, even if it's small, because small things have a way of getting large before the pile's empty.

speaker: a009
text: I'm tired, and that's the honest answer — not tired of this room or the two of you, but tired in my bones in a way I didn't feel at thirty or even forty, and Dav starved at forty-six and I am forty-seven, and some mornings that arithmetic sits on my chest before I've said a word to anyone. I'll take my two from the pile and I'll stand when I need to stand. But I want Dell to know that what she's been doing for me these past years isn't something I've stopped feeling, even when I'm quiet.

speaker: a010
text: Ryn, forty-seven is not forty-six — Dav was Dav and you are you, and the pile's got fifteen today instead of nothing. Take your two and eat them tonight, and stop doing that arithmetic alone.

speaker: a011
text: Ryn, I hear what you said and I'm holding it — but I want you to promise me right now that if you feel that bone-tiredness getting heavier before the year closes, you say it in this room before you say it to no one, because I am not watching you go the way Dav went without a fight. Roan's right that forty-seven isn't forty-six, but what keeps it that way is you eating tonight and me knowing when you need another one from my stores. That's not a gift, that's a standing arrangement, and I need to hear you say it back.

speaker: a010
text: Ryn, say it back to her — she needs the words, not just the nod. Dell's kept more people breathing in this village than anyone wants to count, and the least you can give her for that is the promise she's asking for.

speaker: a011
text: Ryn, I'm not closing this room until I hear you say it back — you said you feel what I've done for you, so prove it by naming the arrangement out loud, because a promise said in words is the kind of thing I can hold onto when you go quiet again.

speaker: a009
text: If it gets heavier, I'll say it in this room before I say it anywhere else — that's the arrangement, and it stands. Dell, go to the pile first this morning; I'll be two steps behind you.

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).

speaker: a007
text: Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).

speaker: a015
text: Fina takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 5).

speaker: a003
text: Esa takes 1 from the pile (pile now 4).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 4 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a015
text: Fina gathers Eron to talk.

speaker: a015
text: Pile's gone and I've got fourteen — you're at eighteen, so between us we're solid, but Kael's sitting dry and Roan's got nothing again and I don't want either of them going thin before year-end. I'll cover Roan if you can spare a look toward Kael — he's one of the names Father kept close and I'm not ready to let that go. How are you sitting on Zinn and Nessa?

speaker: a012
text: Kael gets one from me today, no question — he's stood in the right place every time it mattered and I won't let him go dry. Zinn and Nessa both ate, I made sure of it; Nessa's thin but above the line, and Zinn's got Mako watching her which I trust halfway. What I don't have a clean read on is Mako taking six from the pile — same move as last year, and this time there's no Bram to draw everyone's eyes away from it.

speaker: a015
text: Mako taking six when the pile was already thin is a problem — that's not a man sharing a lean year, that's a man building a cushion on everyone else's back. I don't want to move on him without knowing who else read it the same way, but if Kael and Roan see what we see, that's a conversation worth having before he does it again next year.

speaker: a012
text: Kael and Roan both went without from the pile — they read it the same way we do, I'd stake food on that. Before we bring them into a room together, though, I want to know one thing from you: Zinn's Mako's blood and she's been solid with us, but if this village has a conversation about Mako's taking, she's standing in two places at once — have you had any feel for which way she'd lean if it came to a real choice?

speaker: a015
text: Zinn's been good to us — gave food to Nessa when she didn't have to, and she's got eyes; she knows what Mako is. But knowing and choosing when it's your own blood on the other side of it are two different things, and I wouldn't count on her until I'd heard it from her own mouth first.

speaker: a012
text: Then I'll go to Zinn before I go to Kael — not to put her in a corner, just to talk as blood, and let her say it herself. If she can't say it, that's an answer too.

speaker: a015
text: That's the right move — go quiet and let her find her own words, because if you push she'll say what she thinks you want to hear and that's worth nothing. Whatever she tells you, come back to me before you take it anywhere else; I want to hear her answer in your words before we decide whether Kael comes into this.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Eron to talk.

speaker: a014
text: Eron, I held zero food going into year-end and I didn't starve — but this year the pile went dry before I got a single grain, and I'm sitting at nothing again while Mako took six and Vela took four. Tell me what you're carrying, because if we're both thin we need to figure that out now, not when it's too late.

speaker: a012
text: Zinn, I'm at eighteen — you're not going to starve, not while I'm holding that. But I need to hear something from you first: Mako's your blood and he just took six from a pile that left you with nothing — what does that tell you about where he's counting you in his plan?

speaker: a014
text: It tells me he's counting himself first and trusting I'll manage — and maybe I would have, but I didn't get the chance to find out, and a man who takes six while his daughter holds nothing hasn't earned the benefit of the doubt twice. Give me two food, Eron. I'll eat, I'll keep watching him, and we'll talk more before anyone else does.

speaker: a012
text: Two food, take it — and I believe what you said about Mako, but I need to hear it again when the hunger isn't talking, because the words a person says when they're full carry more weight than the words they say when they're empty.

speaker: a014
text: Two food and I hear you — when I'm fed and thinking clear I'll tell you the same thing, because it's true whether my belly's empty or not. What I want you to think on while I eat is this: Mako took six, Vela took four, and neither of them left anything for people who were watching the pile same as them — that's two people deciding the village owes them a living, and if that's the shape of things now, we need to know who else in that circle is counting that way.

speaker: a012
text: Vela I can half-explain — she's old, she's been feeding Taric for years and Taric's gone now, and a woman who's been giving out of her store for that long has earned a right to fill it back up. But six for Mako with you standing there empty-handed isn't the same kind of math, and yeah, I want to know if he talked to Vela before the pile opened, because two people moving fast and heavy on the same morning can look like coincidence and not be.

speaker: a014
text: If Mako talked to Vela before the pile opened, we'd need to see it happen twice to be sure — one morning could be anything. What I know is that Vela's been generous when she had reason to be, and a woman like that doesn't start moving greedy unless someone told her the ground had changed. I want to watch how they stand near each other today before I decide what this morning meant.

speaker: a015
text: Fina gives 1 food to Roan.

speaker: a010
text: Roan gives 1 food to Eron.

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Mako, Ryn, Roan, Eron, Nessa, Zinn, Fina to talk.

speaker: a004
text:
Taric is dead.

That needs saying plain before anything else, because he was the last man in this village I trusted without counting, and now I am counting everyone in this room.

The pile gave fifteen for twelve of us and it's gone — Mako took six, Vela took four, and I took none, so someone in this circle is already thinking about next year while I'm still standing here thinking about last night.

speaker: a014
text: Taric fed Vela through lean years and died holding nothing — that's a man who gave until there was nothing left to give, and this room should sit with that before it moves on to counting. Mako, six food from a pile of fifteen for twelve people isn't hunger, it's a decision, and I want to hear you name what it was.

speaker: a013
text: Mako took six and Vela took four and I'm sitting on one — I don't need to do the math out loud for this room to understand what that means for me. I'll hold my tongue on Vela for now because Taric just died and she fed him when she had no reason to, but Mako, Zinn asked you a clean question and so will I: was that six for yourself, or was some of it counted toward someone else before you reached the pile?

speaker: a004
text: Mako, I've watched you move quiet for ten years and plant roots in half the households in this village — Eron, Nessa, Zinn — and now you've pulled six food from a common pile while three people in this room are sitting on nothing. That's not hunger and it's not coincidence. Name the number you think is yours, or this room names it for you.

speaker: a008
text: Zinn is my daughter and I pulled for both of us — two of those six were already hers in my head before I reached the pile, and I've already given her what I owe. The rest kept me eating after two years of going thin, and I'll stand behind that in front of anyone in this room.

speaker: a003
text: Mako, you named Zinn and you named your own thin years — I'll give you that much — but four food for one man with daughters who can feed themselves is still four, and Kael is sitting empty and Nessa is sitting on one, and those are the numbers this room is going to remember when next year's pile opens.

speaker: a008
text: Kael, you took none and you're still standing — tell me what you need and I'll give you one food right now, in front of this room, so that account is open before anyone walks out. The four I kept are mine after two years of going thin; I'm not ashamed of eating, but I'm not blind to who's empty either.

speaker: a009
text: Mako, one food in front of this room is the right start, but Kael's empty and I'm empty and Nessa's sitting on one — three of us walked away from a pile of fifteen with nothing or close to it, and "one food right now" doesn't explain six. I'm not asking you to starve; I'm asking you to name what "fair" looks like to you before the next pile opens, because a number said out loud in this circle is the kind of thing that holds when the year gets long.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn named the thing I've been holding — a number said out loud is the only kind that holds. Mako, I'll take your one food for Kael as good faith, but before this circle breaks I want to hear you say what you think one person's share is when fifteen lands for twelve, because I'll be counting next year and so will everyone else in this room.

speaker: a013
text: Mako's already committed one food to Kael in front of this room and that's a thing I'll hold him to — but the question Ryn and Esa are asking is the one that matters, and I want to hear him answer it before this circle decides it's satisfied. Mako, fifteen for twelve is one and a quarter food each; name a cap you'd hold to next year, out loud, and this room will remember you said it.

speaker: a008
text: Two food per person is the number I'll name — that's the cap I'll hold to next year, out loud, in this room, and I'll give Kael his food now to close the account I opened. If the pile runs short and two each leaves someone empty, we deal with that as a village, same as we've always had to.

speaker: a003
text: Two is a number I can hold in my head when the pile opens. I'll remember you said it — this room will remember — and if you stand to it next year, that counts for something with me.

speaker: a002
text: Mako, I'll hold that number too — two food is the rule this circle just made, and I want Kael to hear me say it out loud before he takes your food and before anyone decides it was charity instead of a debt this village is collecting. Taric died empty after feeding half this room and I'm not going to let the lesson in that go quiet before the year's halfway done.

speaker: a003
text: Taric died empty and I stood beside him for ten years and couldn't put food in his hands at the end — that's the thing I'm carrying out of this room, and I want this circle to carry it too. Mako, I'll hold your two-food rule the same as Vela will, and Kael, when the pile opens next year I'll be watching to see who reaches first and how many times.

speaker: a014
text: Two food is the rule and this room just made it, and I'll hold to it — but I want Vela to say the same number out loud before we close, because she took four this morning same as Mako took six, and a rule that only binds the man who got named first isn't a rule, it's a grudge.

speaker: a015
text: Vela, Zinn's right — say the number, because this room just held Mako to it and you walked out with four, and I'd rather hear it from you clean than carry the question into next year.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, Fina and Zinn are right and so is the room — say two, out loud, or this circle just made a rule that bends around whoever's standing closest to the pile when it opens.

speaker: a008
text: Vela, I'll wait the same breath the room waited on me — say two, or tell us the number you think is yours, because a rule with one name on it is just a story someone tells later to explain why they reached first.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, I've got breath left in me to wait, but not all year — say the number or this room closes without you in the circle, and you know what that means when Dell and Ryn are the ones deciding who stands next.

speaker: a009
text: Vela, I've watched this room hold Mako to a number and I'll watch it hold you to one — say two, or tell us why Taric's memory deserves a different rule than the one we just named in his honor.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, I've been in this room since year two waiting on a straight answer from you, and I'm still waiting — say two, or walk out, because the rule this circle made has your name on it the same as Mako's and the whole room just heard Taric's name spoken over it.

speaker: a007
text: Vela, this room has been patient and so have I, but I've got two food and a satiation I'm not proud of, and I will not let Taric's death become the story of a rule that had room carved out for you at the end. Say two.

speaker: a015
text: Vela, the whole room is waiting and I'm one of them — say two, or tell us right now what number you think fits a woman who watched Taric give himself dry, because I've got no patience left for silence on this.

speaker: a009
text: Vela, every person in this room has already said the word — I've said it, Mako's said it, Esa's said it, Kael's said it, Zinn said it first — and you are the only one left standing behind your own silence. Say two, or tell us the number you'll hold to, because this room doesn't close with a gap where your answer should be.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, you already said two — I heard you say it before Zinn pushed — so I'm not sure what we're all still waiting on, but if this room needs to hear it a second time to believe it, then say it a second time, because I'd rather close this clean than leave a crack for someone to wedge open later.

speaker: a013
text: Vela said two and Kael heard it — I heard it too, and I'll hold her to it the same as I'll hold Mako. What I want before this room breaks is one thing settled: Kael is sitting empty and I'm sitting on one, and neither of us can eat on a rule, so Mako, give Kael that food now while we're all watching, because a promise made in front of witnesses is only as good as the moment it's kept.

speaker: a002
text: Two. I said it and I'll say it again so every person in this room has heard it with their own ears and can't be told later that they misremembered. Mako, give Kael his food now — that's the only thing left that needs doing before this circle is worth anything.

speaker: a013
text: Mako, the room's watching — give Kael the food you promised, and do it before this circle starts wondering whether a promise made in front of witnesses means the same thing to you as it does to everyone else here.

speaker: a008
text:
Kael, here's your food — take it.

That's the account closed and the rule standing, and everyone in this room just watched both happen at once.

speaker: a007
text: Kael's fed and the rule's named, and I'll carry both of those into next year — but I want to say one thing before this room walks out: Taric died empty and Bram died empty, and this village is down to twelve people, and I've got three children in this room who are going to be here after I'm gone, so whatever we just built, we build it to last.

speaker: a008
text: Sela's right that we're twelve now, and twelve is the number we protect — but I want to name one thing this room should carry past today: the pile rule holds for everyone, but it only holds if the people in this room are still here to enforce it, so if anyone's sitting thin going into next year, say so before the year gets long, not after.

speaker: a004
text:
I take the food from Mako's hand and close my fingers around it.

Twelve people and a rule that held in front of witnesses — that's more than I had this morning. I want this circle to meet before the pile opens next year, not after, because the only time the rule matters is before someone's already reached.

speaker: a007
text: Kael, I'll be at that meeting before the pile opens — but I want to name something this room hasn't said yet: I'm sitting on two food and my satiation is low, which means I need to eat well this year or I won't be standing here to enforce anything. If anyone in this circle has food to spare before year's end, I'm not too proud to say I need it.

speaker: a002
text: Sela, I've got eight food and I can spare one for you — I'll give it before the day's out, because a circle that loses another body to starvation isn't a circle anymore, it's a warning. The meeting before the pile opens is the thing I want locked in now, not as a suggestion but as a date everyone in this room commits to, because last year we named a rule after the pile was already empty and that's too late.

speaker: a009
text: I'm standing here with nothing in my hands and a satiation that won't last the year, so I'll say it plain before this room closes: I need food from someone who can spare it, and I'm asking in front of witnesses so no one has to wonder later whether I said it or swallowed it. Vela, you named eight — I'm not asking for more than one.

speaker: a004
text: Ryn, I'll give you one food before the day's out — not because I trust you the way I once did, but because you're standing in this circle saying it out loud and that's worth something. Vela, hold your food for Sela; I've got one now and I can spare it from Mako's gift.

speaker: a002
text: Ryn, I'll still give you one from my eight — Kael's one food shouldn't have to stretch two ways, and I'd rather be known as the woman who fed this room than the one who counted while people went empty. Sela, you'll have yours before nightfall as well. Eight is enough to be generous and still sleep fed.

speaker: a013
text: I'm sitting on one food with satiation that already slipped last year, and I'll say it the same way Ryn said it — plainly, in front of this room: I need one food from someone who can spare it before the year runs long. I've got a daughter in this circle and I intend to still be here when she needs me.

speaker: a007
text: Vela, I'll take you up on that food before nightfall — and Nessa, I've got two food and you're my blood, so one of mine is already yours. Don't any of you let this room walk out before the thin ones are fed, because a circle that enforces a rule on Mako and then watches Nessa starve is a circle that doesn't mean what it said.

speaker: a002
text: Sela's already moved to feed Nessa, which is the thing that tells me this room has more spine than the last ten years gave it credit for. I'll give Ryn her food before nightfall and Sela hers, and then I want every person here to think hard about what twelve becomes if we lose another body to a lean year — because eleven enforces that rule with a lot less weight than twelve does.

speaker: a007
text: Eron, Nessa, Zinn — I'm looking at all three of you when I say this: Vela just offered to feed me and I already gave Nessa mine, which means this circle is doing the thing we built it to do, and I need you to remember that when the pile opens next year and someone reaches early and the temptation is to wait and see. We don't wait and see. We move together, same breath, same step.

speaker: a013
text: Sela, I hear you — same breath, same step — and I'll be at that meeting before the pile opens, same as Kael. But I need to say it plain while this room is still whole: Eron is sitting on nineteen food and hasn't said a word in this circle about feeding anyone thin, and that's a silence I'd rather name here than wonder about later.

speaker: a007
text: Eron, Nessa just said your name out loud in front of this whole room, and she's not wrong — nineteen food and silence while your sisters and Ryn and Kael went thin isn't something I can explain for you, so I need to hear you explain it yourself.

speaker: a002
text: Eron, I've fed people in this room and I've held my tongue when I should have spoken, but nineteen food while Nessa sat on one and Ryn walked away empty is not a thing I can explain for you either — so say it now, in front of the same witnesses who heard Mako say two and watched him hand Kael his food, because this circle doesn't close with that number unaddressed.
